title: feat(editor): add getSelectedText(), multi-line list toggle, and atomic replaceRange

commits.message:
feat(editor): add getSelectedText(), multi-line list toggle, and atomic replaceRange

Three selection-model gaps share one root cause: list commands and the
API both assumed cursor-only positions where a full anchor/head range
was already available.

getSelectedText() was absent from EditorAPI, forcing callers to manually
slice getDocument() between raw anchor/head coordinates. The new method
uses view.state.doc.sliceString() so reversed selections normalize
automatically without extra caller logic.

toggleOrderedList and toggleUnorderedList read only anchor, silently
discarding head. Any multi-line selection collapsed to a single-line
operation. getLinesInRange() and applyLines() replace the cursor-only
assumption; semantics follow VS Code and Obsidian (mixed state toggles
on, column-0 boundary excluded, reversed selection normalized).

replaceRange(from, to, insert, selection?, opts?) is a new EditorAPI
primitive that emits a single CM6 transaction for both the range edit
and the resulting selection. The old applyLines dispatched setDocument
then setSelection separately — two transactions, two undo entries.
Pressing Ctrl+Z once reverted only the selection move, leaving the
document in a half-toggled state. replaceRange fixes this: one Ctrl+Z
fully reverts the entire toggle. This matches the pattern already used
by markdown-keymap.ts and markdown-autopair.ts inside core.

toggleHeading and toggleBlockquote remain cursor-based intentionally:
Markdown headings have no multi-line form, and blockquote toggling
conventionally targets the current paragraph.
